extracted.intended_audience: funding agency staff, researchers and administrators studying peer review and grant-evaluation processes
extracted.subtask_description: Retrospective analysis of factors that influence assignment of scientific-merit scores for cardiovascular grant-in-aid applications, examining internal and external reviewer scores, committee effects, and temporal trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal reviewer scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores assigned by internal reviewers and their relationship to the final committee score (single internal reviewer correlation r = 0.331; mean internal score impact on final committee score r2 = 0.607, P < 0.001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regression analysis in the study found that mean internal score had a greater impact on final committee score than external reviewer scores; internal reviewer scores were more closely correlated to the final committee assessment of scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: External reviewer scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores assigned by external reviewers and their relationship to the final committee score (poor correlation between external reviewers and final outcomes: r = 0.113; external scores' impact on final score r2 = 0.348, P < 0.001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviewer scores showed low correlation with final committee scores and explained less variance in committee outcomes than internal reviewer scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined mean of internal and external scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis using the mean of internal and external reviewer scores (correlation with final committee score improved to r = 0.451; agreement beyond chance was only moderate: weighted Cohen's kappa = 0.532).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averaging internal and external scores increases correlation with committee outcomes but inter-rater agreement remains only moderate, indicating combined reviewer means do not fully predict committee decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final committee score / influence of committee discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Final committee-assigned scientific merit score, which differed significantly from individual internal or external reviewer scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The observed significant differences between final committee scores and individual reviewer scores suggest that committee discussion and deliberation are important and highly influential steps in determining final outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee assignment effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of which review committee handled the application: when entered as a dummy variable it was statistically significant (P < 0.001) but explained less than 8% of the variance in final committee score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different committees produce statistically different outcomes, but committee identity accounts for only a small portion of variability in final scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year of application / temporal trends in scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporal change in scoring over the study period: mean scores showed a small 'upward creep' across five years, explaining less than 4% of variance in final committee score (r2 = 0.039, P < 0.001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is modest inflation or upward drift in mean scores over time, but its effect on final outcomes is minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures of agreement and statistical metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of quantitative statistics to evaluate relationships and agreement: Pearson correlation coefficients (r), weighted Cohen's kappa (agreement beyond chance), regression R-squared (r2) and P-values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics are employed to quantify correlation, inter-rater agreement, and the proportion of variance in final committee scores explained by reviewer scores, committee identity, and year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness / sample inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion criterion for analysis: of 804 submitted proposals, 779 had complete data and were included in the retrospective study (1990–1994).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses were restricted to complete cases; completeness of reviewer/committee data is necessary for the applied correlation and regression analyses.
